dedupe_keys.name: physrisk os climate physical climate risk library

description: Physrisk is an open-source physical climate risk calculation engine for assessing the effects of climate change on large numbers of individual assets, including natural assets, and operations, and the potential benefit of resilience measures. It runs bottom-up calculations that combine hazard indicators, on-boarded from public resources or inferred from climate projections such as CMIP and CORDEX in a companion hazard repository, with vulnerability models of assets and operations, to estimate financial risks or socio-economic impacts. It is an OS-Climate project; OS-Climate merged with the Fintech Open Source Foundation under the Linux Foundation in June 2024. It is not limited to a region: coverage follows the hazard indicators loaded, typically global climate scenario grids. The library is installed from PyPI as physrisk-lib, is Apache 2.0 licensed and free, and can also be hosted, with an example API and user interface in separate repositories and online documentation of the methodology. Caveats: vulnerability models are simplified and asset-class specific, hazard indicators inherit the resolution and bias of their sources, and results are meant for screening. It serves climate adaptation and hazard exposure screening of infrastructure portfolios, such as power plants and real estate; related records are CLIMADA, the CDS CMIP6 projections, NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 and Delft-FIAT.
